headline: PRO FARMER WRAPS; CATTLE ON FEED AT 2 PM
subheadline: Tour scouts found a smaller bean crop than last year, corn held steady, and now the livestock market waits on Cattle on Feed.
lead: Pro Farmer's tour wrapped Thursday with pod counts running below year-ago in key areas, and the bean board yawned: November beans at **$12.33**, up roughly 7 cents on the day but still 6 cents short of the $12.39 call level -- an overbought market that got good news and still couldn't close the gap. December corn at **$5.03** is the cleaner story, sitting comfortably above the $4.90 weekly-thread line ahead of Cattle on Feed at 2 PM CT.
the_takeaway: Tour confirmed a smaller bean crop; the market already knew. Cattle on Feed decides the afternoon.
teaser: Pro Farmer found fewer bean pods than last year. The board shrugged. Cattle on Feed at 2 PM is the real test.

one_number.unit: head/day of processing capacity still offline
one_number.context: The Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, continues removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity. Now a new wrinkle: Tyson's Joslin, Illinois closure is pulling additional kill capacity from a market that was already packer-constrained, not supply-constrained.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans up toward $12.39; November beans closed today at $12.32, up but short of the line.
yesterdays_call.note: Right direction, wrong level. The overbought read that capped Thursday's close capped today's too.

sections.title: TOUR WRAPS: BEANS HOLD, WHEAT SLIPS
sections.body:
- Pro Farmer scouts reported below-year-ago pod counts in key areas, but November beans at **$12.32** added only 3¾ cents; the board's been pricing a tighter crop for weeks and the tour didn't reset that calculus.
- Wheat gave back 7 cents to $6.79, the sharpest single-day pullback of the week, as no fresh demand news emerged to hold the gains built on earlier Hormuz headlines.
- Corn held, December at $5.03, up less than 2 cents; the ethanol complex is gearing up for harvest flow, and the Iowa plant news confirms the pipeline is clearing space for above-average supply.
sections.catalyst: Pro Farmer tour concluded; pod counts below year-ago in several states, tour national number due today.
sections.bottom_line: Tour gave beans a story without giving them a new leg. Wheat ran out of Hormuz fuel.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: tour confirmed tighter pods, price barely moved. Overbought read still capping follow-through.

sections.title: CATTLE ON FEED: 2 PM IS THE MOMENT
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$223.43** ticked up 0.2% in positioning trade ahead of the Cattle on Feed report at 2 PM CT; the fed trade hasn't reset since last month's number, and today's report is the line the next leg depends on.
- Feeders at $335.43 eased 0.3%, and the screwworm story just got complicated: a confirmed case in Sonora, Mexico puts the Aug. 24 Douglas, AZ port reopening in doubt, which means the feeder supply tightness that drove this rally may not unwind on schedule.
- Tyson's Joslin, Illinois closure is adding a new processing-capacity hole on top of the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19; the market is packer-constrained at both ends now.
sections.catalyst: USDA Cattle on Feed due 2:00 PM CT; screwworm confirmed in Sonora, threatens Aug. 24 port reopening; Tyson Joslin closure adding capacity pressure.
sections.bottom_line: The screwworm case in Sonora is the sleeper: if Aug. 24 slips, the feeder supply story gets a second act.
sections.farmer_action: If you are backgrounding feeders with Mexican supply assumptions baked in: the Sonora screwworm case puts Aug. 24 at risk. Do not price that supply into your break-even until USDA confirms the port schedule holds.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: port reopening, already conditional, now has a new threat. Feeder supply story extends.

sections.title: CRUDE FIRMS ON IRAN SUPPLY SQUEEZE
sections.body:
- WTI at **$87.21** added 0.9%, on pace for a second straight weekly gain; Iranian crude cargoes to Chinese independent refiners have nearly dried up following reinstated U.S. sanctions, and China's oil imports are set to rise roughly 1.2 million barrels per day in Q4 as buyers hunt replacement supply.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern of escalation and deflation running since spring, is entering a new phase: this time the supply squeeze is at the cargo level, not the chokepoint, which makes it stickier than a headline risk premium.
- Natural gas added 1.5% to $2.79, still historically cheap at the bottom of its 52-week range; input costs for fall fieldwork remain manageable.
sections.catalyst: Iranian oil cargoes to China nearly dried up; China Q4 import rebound of 1.2M bbl/day reported; oil prices heading for second straight weekly gain.
sections.bottom_line: Iranian supply squeeze is a cargo story now, not a Hormuz story. That makes the crude bid more durable.

outside_the_pit.title: Screwworm Case in Sonora Threatens Aug. 24 Port Reopening
outside_the_pit.body: A confirmed screwworm case in Sonora, Mexico puts the first phased reopening at Douglas, AZ in serious doubt. If the port date slips, the feeder supply tightness that has been priced into the rally all summer does not unwind on schedule, and break-even math for fall placements needs a second look.

outside_the_pit.title: Tyson Joslin Closure Leaves Thousands of Illinois Cattle Unplaced
outside_the_pit.body: The abrupt Tyson closure in Joslin, Illinois is leaving thousands of head without a processing home, adding a new capacity hole alongside the Cargill lockout. The industry was already over-capacity in processing but under-capacity in active kill; this deepens the packer-margin problem heading into fall runs.

weekly_thread.question: What will Pro Farmer scouts find, and does the tour push December corn above $4.90 or back below $4.75 by Friday?
weekly_thread.status_text: Scouts found below-year-ago bean pod counts; December corn settled at $5.03, well above the $4.90 line. The tour pushed corn up, not down. Question resolved: corn above $4.90.

the_more_you_know.title: Phosphate from Morocco: what the first shipment in 5 years means for input costs
the_more_you_know.body: The first Moroccan phosphate shipment to the U.S. in five years just landed under temporary countervailing duty relief. Morocco holds roughly 70% of the world's known phosphate reserves. If the CVD relief holds, it opens a non-China, non-Russia supply lane for fertilizer heading into 2027 planning season, a meaningful optionality shift for input-cost risk.

watch_list.desc: USDA Cattle on Feed: placement above 105% of year-ago is bearish for deferred contracts; on-feed inventory above 100% extends the packer-margin squeeze.
Douglas, AZ port reopening: now conditional on screwworm containment in Sonora. A delay keeps feeder supply tight and the feeder/live spread wide.
Weekly Export Sales: corn above 500K MT confirms demand is absorbing the big crop; beans above 300K MT says China purchases are holding pace.
USDA Crop Progress: corn dough/dent progress and soybean pod-fill ratings after Pro Farmer's tour. Any rating decline below 60% good-to-excellent reopens the yield debate.

daily_quote.text: The cure for high prices is high prices. The cure for low prices is low prices.

source_summary: CME Group settlement prices; USDA Cattle on Feed (2:00 PM CT, report not yet released); Pro Farmer Crop Tour (Aug. 17-20); Brownfield Ag News; Drovers; OilPrice.com; Feedstuffs; AgWeb; EIA
